RIGHT BREAST, WIRE LOCALIZED EXCISION FOR CALCIFICATIONS: 
DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU, cribriform and clinging types (intermediate 
nuclear grade) associated with columnar hyperplasia with atypia, is 
present in a 0.3cm area in 1 of 32 blocks (block 14; levels examined). 
No calcifications or necrosis are seen. 
DCIS is < 0.1cm from the anterior margin. 
Severely atypical ductal hyperplasia is present in block 3 (papillary 
pattern, 0.2cm area, not close to margins, levels examined) and block 8 
(cribriform pattern with calcifications; 0.2cm area, not close to 
margins, levels examined). 
LOBULAR CARCINOMA IN SITU is present. 
Calcifications are associated with adenosis and cysts. 
Note: The entire specimen is examined microscopically. 
The area of DCIS and the two areas of ADH have different histologic 
appearances. Dr. James Connolly reviewed slide 14 and concurs with the 
diagnosis of DCIS. 
The DCIS appears to be an incidental finding and was not present in the 
area of the radiologic calcifications. 
This carcinoma would be classified as AJCC (6th edition) Tis NX MX. 
LEFT BREAST BIOPSY, WIRE LOCALIZED EXCISION FOR CALCIFICATIONS: 
Atypical lobular hyperplasia. 
One lymph node with no tumor seen. 
Skeletal muscle. 
Note: The radiologic calcifications were not present in this specimen 
(see below). All fibrous tissue was examined microscopically. 
LEFT BREAST, RE-EXCISION: 
Epithelial hyperplasia. 
Calcifications are associated with benign epithelium. 
Note: The radiologic calcifications were not present in this specimen 
(see below). All fibrous tissue was examined microscopically. 
LEFT BREAST, RE-EXCISION: 
DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU, cribriform type (intermediate nuclear grade) is 
present in 1 of 11 blocks (0.2cm area, block 56, levels examined). No 
necrosis or calcifications are seen. The DCIS is associated with columnar 
hyperplasia with atypia and mucin production. 
DCIS is > 0.3cm from all margins. 
Atypical lobular hyperplasia is present. 
Skeletal muscle is present. 
Calcifications are associated with columnar hyperplasia and apocrine 
cysts. 
Note: Radiologic calcifications are present in this specimen and are 
associated with benign epithelium. The DCIS appears to be an incidental 
finding. Slide 56 was also reviewed by Dr. James Connolly who concurs 
with this interpretation. 
This patient has bilateral DCIS which would be classified as AJCC 
(6th edition) Tis NX MX.
